*   The sanitizeRoute function must be a named export from packages/insomnia/src/konnect/transform.ts.

*   When the route contains no template syntax, sanitizeRoute must return the route object unchanged (equal by value).

*   sanitizeRoute must strip {{ ... }} expressions (including their delimiters) from the name field, leaving surrounding text intact. For example, 'Route {{ env.SECRET }}' becomes 'Route '.

*   sanitizeRoute must strip {{ ... }} expressions from each entry in the paths array, keeping any surrounding text. For example, '/api/{{ env.SECRET }}/users' becomes '/api//users'.

*   sanitizeRoute must strip {{ ... }} expressions from each entry in the hosts array, keeping any surrounding text. For example, '{{ env.SECRET }}.test.com' becomes '.test.com'.

*   For the methods array: entries that are entirely a {{ ... }} expression (so the full string is stripped to empty) must be filtered out. If all entries are removed, the methods field must be set to null. If some entries remain non-empty after stripping, only those valid entries are kept.

*   For the headers object: any header entry whose value array becomes entirely empty after stripping must be dropped from the returned headers object. Any header entry whose key/name becomes entirely empty after stripping must also be dropped.

*   sanitizeRoute must strip {% ... %} block tag syntax from string fields, in addition to {{ ... }} variable syntax.

*   sanitizeRoute must handle delimiter interleaving: a {% %} tag nested inside {{ }} syntax must be stripped, and a {{ }} tag nested inside {% %} syntax must also be stripped, preventing template injection via interleaved delimiters.

*   Unpaired delimiters (an opening {{ or {% with no corresponding closing delimiter) must be left intact and not modified.

*   sanitizeRoute must strip {{ ... }} expressions from the expression field, keeping surrounding text intact.

*   sanitizeRoute must handle null values for name, methods, paths, hosts, headers, and expression fields without throwing an error, returning those fields as null in the result.

Done. I implemented `sanitizeRoute` as a named export in `packages/insomnia/src/konnect/transform.ts:266`.

## Approach

The core is a small helper, `stripTemplateSyntax`, that strips Nunjucks syntax by repeatedly removing the **innermost** tag until the string stabilizes:

```ts
const INNERMOST_VARIABLE = /\{\{(?:(?!\{\{|\{%|\}\}|%\}).)*\}\}/g;
const INNERMOST_BLOCK    = /\{%(?:(?!\{\{|\{%|\}\}|%\}).)*%\}/g;
```

Both patterns use a *tempered* body that forbids any delimiter inside the match, so a match can never span a nested tag. Looping inside-out is what handles the interleaving/injection cases: `{{ {% p %} }}` first loses the inner `{% p %}`, then the now-innermost `{{  }}` — and vice versa. Because an unpaired opening never has a matching close, it simply never matches and is left intact.

`sanitizeRoute` then applies it per field:
- **name / expression** — stripped, surrounding text kept.
- **paths / hosts** — each entry stripped (no filtering, so `/api//users` is preserved).
- **methods** — entries stripped, empty ones dropped; field becomes `null` if none remain.
- **headers** — an entry is dropped when its key strips to empty, or when every value strips to empty.
- Any `null` field stays `null`; `id`, `protocols`, `snis`, `service` pass through unchanged.

## Verification
- Existing suite: 51/51 pass.
- A throwaway 12-case scratch test (removed afterward, `tests/` untouched) exercised every listed requirement — the `{{ }}`/`{% %}` examples, both interleaving directions, unpaired delimiters, methods-to-null, header dropping, and null-safety — all pass.
- `tsc` reports no errors for the file.

+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
+import { sanitizeRoute } from './packages/insomnia/src/konnect/transform';
+
+const base = { id: 'r', protocols: ['http'], snis: null, service: null, name: null, methods: null, paths: null, hosts: null, headers: null, expression: null } as any;
+
+describe('sanitizeRoute', () => {
+  it('unchanged when no template', () => {
+    const r = { ...base, name: 'Route', paths: ['/a'], hosts: ['h.com'] };
+    expect(sanitizeRoute(r)).toEqual(r);
+  });
+  it('strips name', () => { expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, name: 'Route {{ env.SECRET }}'}).name).toBe('Route '); });
+  it('strips paths', () => { expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, paths: ['/api/{{ env.SECRET }}/users']}).paths).toEqual(['/api//users']); });
+  it('strips hosts', () => { expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, hosts: ['{{ env.SECRET }}.test.com']}).hosts).toEqual(['.test.com']); });
+  it('methods filter + null', () => {
+    expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, methods: ['{{x}}']}).methods).toBe(null);
+    expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, methods: ['GET', '{{x}}']}).methods).toEqual(['GET']);
+  });
+  it('headers drop empty value/key', () => {
+    expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, headers: {'X-Real-IP': ['{{ env.SECRET }}']}}).headers).toEqual({});
+    expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, headers: {'{{ env.SECRET }}': ['v']}}).headers).toEqual({});
+    expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, headers: {'X-Foo': ['bar']}}).headers).toEqual({'X-Foo': ['bar']});
+  });
+  it('block tags', () => { expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, name: 'a{% if x %}b'}).name).toBe('ab'); });
+  it('interleave {% inside {{', () => { expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, name: 'x{{ {% p %} }}y'}).name).toBe('xy'); });
+  it('interleave {{ inside {%', () => { expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, name: 'x{% {{ p }} %}y'}).name).toBe('xy'); });
+  it('unpaired left intact', () => {
+    expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, name: 'a{{ b'}).name).toBe('a{{ b');
+    expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, name: 'a{% b'}).name).toBe('a{% b');
+  });
+  it('expression', () => { expect(sanitizeRoute({...base, expression: 'http.path == {{ x }}'}).expression).toBe('http.path == '); });
+  it('nulls stay null', () => {
+    const r = sanitizeRoute(base);
+    expect([r.name, r.methods, r.paths, r.hosts, r.headers, r.expression]).toEqual([null,null,null,null,null,null]);
